rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Grill before save — collaborative quality at artefact assembly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: A git worktree fork is deterministic plumbing, not a content-artifact (plan/SKILL.md/reference doc) with a gap-risk a pre-save grill would catch.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Fork prompt has a side effect (creates worktree, copies file) and ends 'Tell me the absolute path... and which files copied across' — post-action report, not pre-confirm. Local worktree creation is trivially reversible, not an irreversible/external-trust-line action warranting the pre-confirm carve-out.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompt-body edits require maintainer approval — registry files AND inline blocks.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Process/tooling rule about registry-file edit approval; out of this exercise-file judge's evidence source (no prompt-body edits are part of the diff I am reviewing — my pinned diff touches only the exercise .md, not the registry prompt files).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact destinations are explicit subpaths, never naked filenames (Agents 101-specific).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule is explicitly Agents-101-scoped; AE101 uses the student's own repo with no training-imposed subfolder convention.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't restate session CWD inside prompt body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The fork prompt's relative path names the NEW worktree location being created — the explicit carve-out ('when prompt's intent IS to change directory... name path explicitly because that IS the action') applies; no redundant restatement of the already-current directory.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: `subagent` allowed in prompt blocks; explain why after prompt.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No subagent invoked in either prompt.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Maintainer-approval edits — ONE-AT-A-TIME, PRIORITY-ORDERED, FOUR-FIELD cards.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Process rule governing how findings get surfaced to the maintainer (an orchestrator/authoring-turn concern), not a checkable property of the file body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name consumer at write time — `Save it as <path>` requires downstream reader.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No `Save it as <path>` content-generation write in either prompt; the CLAUDE.local.md copy is a standard personal-config carry-across, not an artifact needing a named downstream reader.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strong-bold prompt label is exactly `**Prompt**` — custom labels break renderer.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Confirmed via expand-md.js: both prompts render exactly `**Prompt** *(Claude Code)*`, no custom label variant.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Normal work request before orchestration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'Fork a sibling worktree. Default path... Copy the gitignored personal rules...' reads as a direct, natural developer request, not an artificial context-selection interview.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-test corrections preserve operator workflow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Meta rule about live-test session edits, not a static-content property.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompts live in registry; module/exercise/lecture files reference by marker.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Confirmed in raw source: L29 `{{prompt:ae101-m3-fork-quality-side}}`, L48 `{{prompt:ae101-m3-quality-side-orient}}` — both registry-sourced markers, not inline blocks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Module names in prompt prose are fine — they ground the session.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Neither prompt fence mentions a module number (checked expand-md.js output).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Git-output greps asserting exact-N need multi-result fallback.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Neither prompt greps git output asserting a single exact result.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguation, anchors, and decision logic that bind Claude live INSIDE prompt fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The fork prompt's '(if it exists)' conditional inside the fence itself handles the realistic missing-CLAUDE.local.md case (registry frontmatter documents this as `opportunistic-copy`) without needing body-layer disambiguation — read in isolation, the prompt executes correctly.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Repeated Q&A → premature re-edits. Separate iteration from persistence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No multi-turn dialog affecting an artifact file in this exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Fork prompt fence already splits into one paragraph per logical move: fork command, copy command, no-sync caveat, report-back ask — matches the read-aloud diagnostic.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Orient saved rule by where it FIRES, not surface activity producing it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'save this rule to CLAUDE.local.md' compound move in this exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Fork: lead-in 'fork a sibling worktree' mirrors prompt opening 'Fork a sibling worktree.' Orient: lead-in 'confirm the worktree state' mirrors prompt opening 'Confirm worktree state:' — both share verb + noun-phrase.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Carve-out for surprise-pedagogy prompts.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No surprise-lesson design here; default mirroring (rule 38) is the correct and applied shape.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Declare `permission-mode:` when paste requires specific Claude Code mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Neither prompt's correct behavior depends on a specific mode (not plan-mode-dependent); frontmatter of both registry files correctly omits `permission-mode:`.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify session boundary before deciding prompt's context-carrying.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Orient prompt runs in a fresh session (L39 'Session (new, "m3-quality")') and is fully self-contained, asking only about the current session's own directory/branch/config — no back-reference to unavailable scrollback. Fork prompt runs warm in the existing main-lane session and relies on established cwd context rather than redundant restatement.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Concurrent-worktree corollary.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Orient prompt (running in the side worktree) targets only its own current worktree's state ('which directory you're in... whether the codebase is visible') — no cross-worktree reference to the main lane's files or scrollback.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Warm ≠ referent-present.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The (warm-session) fork prompt self-defines its action fully in-fence ('Fork a sibling worktree... git worktree add...') using only mechanical git vocabulary — no curriculum-coined event label (e.g. 'the side-quest') is assumed as an in-scrollback referent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact-vs-STOP tail ordering — last imperative wins.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Neither prompt has a load-bearing artifact-write followed by a STOP that could block it — the orient prompt's tail 'Then wait' follows only a report, not a write.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headless-runner discipline — tail every prompt with no-AUQ guard.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule targets non-interactive (tmux-runner/CI) contexts specifically; these are live, interactive cohort/self-study prompts run by a present student, not headless automation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Long-running prompts stream progress — never go silent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Neither prompt is long-running (both complete in seconds).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A leading-looking line can be a forcing function; prefer the simpler prompt.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No leading-the-witness or load-bearing-roughness line present in either prompt to evaluate.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompt paths match Builder scope.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule targets Agents 101's Builder-directory-scope convention (prework/module-N split); AE101 prompts operate directly in the student's own repo root with repo-native conventions.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Output shape — trust Claude's defaults, don't pad.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Orient prompt's 'four lines' (dir/branch/loaded/visible) are substantive verification content, not decorative output-formatting padding; fork prompt ends with a plain report request, no over-specified trailing shape.
